Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:10:2.hebrew: לא ניחא לי - שתהא שפחה חשובה לי, דשקלה מילי מינאי ואזלא נדיא גבי שבבתאי. משום שהיא חשובה, מצויה לספר עם שכינותיה, ותשמע ממני דברים ותסדר אותם לפני שכינותי, ותתן אותי בפיהם ללעג וקלס:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:10:2.english: It is not satisfactory for me - That I should have an esteemed maidservant, who takes words from me and goes chatting among my neighbors. Because she is of high standing, she frequently converses with her neighbors, and she will hear things from me and recount them before my neighbors, and put me in their mouths for ridicule and derision.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:11:1.hebrew: יתרגם אפי' מדעתיה - בתמיה, שלא כתרגום שלנו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:11:1.english: May he translate even according to his own understanding? - [This is asked] in astonishment: [Could it mean] not according to our translation?

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:11:2.hebrew: המתרגם פסוק כצורתו - שבא לחסר תוספת התרגום שלנו, לומר: ״לא אתרגם פסוק זה אלא כצורתו״, כגון ״לא תענה על ריב״ (שמות כג) — ״לא תסהיד על דינא״ — הרי זה בדאי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:11:2.english: One who translates a verse according to its [literal] form - [This refers to one] who comes to omit the addition of our translation, saying, "I will not translate this verse except according to its [literal] form," such as [translating], "You shall not speak in a dispute" (Exodus 23) [as], "You shall not testify in a lawsuit" — behold, this [person] is a liar.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:11:3.hebrew: והמוסיף עליו - שבא לומר: הואיל וניתן רשות להוסיף, אוסיף גם אני בכל מקום שארצה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:11:3.english: And one who adds to it - [One] who comes to say: Since permission was given to add, I too will add wherever I wish.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:11:4.hebrew: הרי זה מחרף - מבזה את המקום, משנה את דבריו. ואונקלוס, כשהוסיף — לא מדעתו הוסיף, שהרי בסיני ניתן, אלא שנשתכח, וחזר ויסדו, כדאמרי' במגילה (דף ג.): ״ושום שכל״ — זה תרגום:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:11:4.english: Behold, he is a reviler - He treats the Omnipresent with contempt [by] altering His words. And Onkelos, when he added [to the text], did not add [it] of his own accord, for [the translation] was given at Sinai; but it was forgotten, and he returned and established it, as we say in Megillah (daf 3a): “'And gave the sense' — this is the translation.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:12:1.hebrew: והני מילי - דסגי בשלשה פסוקים, דאמר לה: ״קריינא״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:12:1.english: And this statement applies - That it suffices with three verses [is] when he said to her: "I am literate."

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:13:1.english: Halakhot - [This refers to a] halakhah [transmitted] to Moses from Sinai.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:13:2.hebrew: תורה - קס"ד תורה שבכתב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:13:2.english: Torah - It entered [the Gemara's] mind [that this means] the Written Torah.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:14:1.hebrew: מדרש - ספרא וספרי, שהן הלכות של [מדרשי] מקראות (ספר ויקרא):
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:14:1.english: Midrash - Sifra and Sifrei, which are the halakhot of [the midrashic expositions of] the verses (the Book of Leviticus).

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:1:1.english: An ordinary document - One made like our [documents].

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:1:2.english: Its witnesses [sign] inside it - Beneath the text.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:1:3.hebrew: מקושר - התם מפרש לה בבבא בתרא, שתקנוהו לכהנים, שאין יכולין להחזיר גרושותיהן. וכשהיו כועסין, הולכין אל הסופר — דממהר לכתוב גט ונותנו לה, ומתחרט לאחר זמן — תקנו להו מקושר, שיש בו טורח לעשותו, ואדהכי והכי מייתבא דעתיה. מניח בראשו שיטה חלק וכותב שיטה, ושיטה חלק וכותב שיטה, וכן עד שלשה או ארבעה או יותר שיטין חלק; וכופל חלק הראשון על הכתב ותופר, וחוזר וכופל חלק השני על שיטת הכתב שתחתיו ותופר, וכן שלישי; והעדים חותמין מבחוץ, בין קשר לקשר. וילפינן התם, דגט פשוט עדיו שנים, מקושר עדיו שלשה; וכל כפל וכפל קרוי קשר, ושלשה קשרין יש בו, ואם בא להרבות קשרים — מרבה בעדים; ושאר טופס השטר כתוב כדרכו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:1:3.english: A tied [document] - There, in [tractate] Bava Batra, [the Gemara] explains that they instituted it for priests, who cannot take back their divorcées. And when they would become angry, they would go to the scribe — who hastens to write a bill of divorce, and [the husband] gives it to her, and after some time he regrets [it] — [therefore] they instituted for them a tied [document], which involves effort to produce it, and in the meantime his mind settles. [The scribe] leaves a blank line at its top and writes a line [of text], and [leaves] a blank line and writes a line [of text], and so on for up to three, four, or more blank lines; and he folds the first blank [line] over the writing and stitches [it], and then folds the second blank [line] over the line of writing beneath it and stitches [it], and so too a third; and the witnesses sign on the outside, between knot and knot. And we learn there that an ordinary document, its witnesses are two; a tied [document], its witnesses are three; and each and every fold is called a “knot,” and it has three knots; and if he wishes to increase [the number of] knots, he increases [the number of] witnesses; and the rest of the text of the document is written in its usual manner.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:1:4.english: Both of them are invalid - Because they were not made in accordance with the enactment of the Sages.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:1:5.hebrew: שיכול לעשותו פשוט - שלא לתפור הקשרים. ואם מפסיק אויר בין שיטות העליונות — מה בכך? וטעמא דת"ק מפרש התם (דף קסד:), דקסבר: אין יכול לעשותו פשוט, מפני שהמקושר והפשוט אין זמנו שוה, שאין כותבין זמן למקושר מאותה שנה, אלא משנה של אחריה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:1:5.english: Because one can transform it into an ordinary [document] - By not sewing the knots. And if empty space separates the upper lines, what of it? And the reasoning of the first Tanna is explained there (Bava Batra 164b): that he holds that one cannot transform it into an ordinary [document], because the date of a tied [document] and an ordinary [document] is not the same, for we do not write the date for a tied [document] from that year, but rather from the year after it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:1:6.hebrew: הכל כמנהג המדינה - מקום שנהגו בפשוט ועשאו מקושר, מקושר ועשאו פשוט — פסול, דכי עבדיה בעל שליח לכתוב, על מנהג המדינה הוא דשויה. ובהאי לא איירי תנאי קמאי, אלא כשאינה במקום עדים. והיינו דהוינן בה: ות"ק לית ליה מנהג המדינה? ומאן פליג עליה בהאי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:1:6.english: Everything is in accordance with regional custom - [In] a place where they were accustomed [to write] an ordinary [document] and he made it tied, [or where they were accustomed to write] a tied [document] and he made it ordinary — [it is] invalid, for when the husband made [the scribe] an agent to write [it], it was according to regional custom that he appointed him. And the earlier Tannaim did not deal with this [issue], but rather with when [the signature] is not in the [designated] place of the witnesses. And this is [the meaning of] what we discuss [in the Gemara]: 'And does the first Tanna not accept regional custom?' For who would dispute him on this?

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:2:1.hebrew: ומשני - ודאי פלוגתא אחריתא היא, ומיהו באתרא דנהיגי כו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:2:1.english: And [the Gemara] answers - Certainly [their] dispute is a different one; however: "In a place where they are accustomed...", etc.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:3:1.english: “Do a simple [task] for me” - An easy errand.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:3:2.hebrew: ועבד מקושר - שליחות כבידה. רשב"ג סבר: מראה מקום הוא לו, דאמר: "די לך בפשוט", וכי עביד מקושר — הואיל ומנהג מדינה אף במקושר — כשר. ותנאי קמאי פליגי עליה, ואמרי: קפידא הוא, ודווקא אמר ליה לעשותו פשוט:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:3:2.english: And made a tied [document] - [This was] a more burdensome agency. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds that he was merely indicating [direction] to him, as he was saying: "An ordinary [document] is sufficient for you"; and when he made a tied [document], since the local custom is also [to use] a tied [document], it is valid. But the first Tannaim disagree with him and say [that] it was an insistence, and he specifically told him to make it ordinary.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:3:3.hebrew: מראה מקום היא לו - שם תמצאנו. ולתנא קמא הוי קפידא: אי איפשי שתקבלנו אלא שם, ואין זה שלוחה במקום אחר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:3:3.english: She is [merely] indicating a place to him - [Meaning:] “There you will find him.” And according to the first tanna, it is an insistence: “I do not want you to receive it except there,” and he is not her agent in another place.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:4:1.hebrew: מראה מקום היא לו - שם תמצאנו. ולתנא קמא הוי קפידא: "אי איפשי שתקבלנו אלא שם", ואין זה שלוחה במקום אחר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:4:1.english: She is indicating a place to him - [Meaning,] there you will find him. But according to the First Tanna, it is an insistence: "I do not want you to receive it anywhere other than there," and this [person] is not her agent in another place.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:5:1.hebrew: בשבח ממון - הוא דאמר ר"ש דאע"פ שהטעה מקודשת, דמסתמא ניחא לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:5:1.english: With enhanced monetary value - It is [in this case] that Rabbi Shimon said that even though he misled [her], she is betrothed, since ordinarily it is agreeable to her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:5:2.hebrew: אבל בשבח יוחסין - על מנת שאני ממזר ונמצא שהוא נתין — לא ניחא לה בשבחו, מפני שהוא מתגאה עליה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:5:2.english: But with enhanced lineage - [Such as where he said:] "On condition that I am a mamzer," and he was found to be a Gibeonite [natin] — she is not pleased with his superior status, because he will act haughtily toward her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:5:3.hebrew: מסאנא דרב מכרעאי - מנעל גדול ממדת רגלי איני חפיצה בו, שאיני יכולה להלך בו. ומשל הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:5:3.english: A shoe that is larger than my foot - A shoe [that is] larger than the size of my foot I do not desire, for I cannot walk in it. And it is a proverb.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:6:1.hebrew: נתין - זה גבעוני, על שם ״ויתנם יהושע חוטבי עצים ושואבי מים״. ואמרי' ביבמות (דף עח:): דוד גזר עליהם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:6:1.english: A natin - This is a Gibeonite, named after [the verse]: “And Joshua made them [vayitnem] hewers of wood and drawers of water” (Joshua 9:27). And we say in Yevamot (78b): David decreed against them [prohibiting them from marrying into the congregation].

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:7:1.english: Grown - Grown, and fit to serve me.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:8:1.hebrew: אלא פליג ברישא - בבבא קמייתא, גבי עני ונמצא עשיר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:8:1.english: Rather, he disagrees in the first clause - In the first clause, regarding [the case of] a poor man and he was found to be wealthy.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:8:2.hebrew: וה"ה - דפליג בבבא בתרייתא גבי שפחה. וכיון דפליג ברישא דאם הטעה לשבח לאו טעותא היא, לא איצטריך למהדר אפלוגי בסיפא. הכי נמי גבי שבח יוחסין לא איצטריך אפלוגי, דפליג ברישא בשבח ממון, וה"ה דפליג בסיפא לשבח יוחסין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:8:2.english: And the same is true - That he disagrees in the latter clause regarding [a] maidservant. And since he disagreed in the first clause, [maintaining] that if he deceived [her] for an improvement it is not a mistake, it was not necessary to repeat his dispute in the latter clause. So too, regarding enhanced lineage, it was not necessary to state his dispute, since he disagreed in the first clause regarding enhanced monetary value, and the same is true that he disagrees in the latter clause with regard to enhanced lineage.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:9:1.english: There - In the case of a grown daughter or maidservant.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:9:2.hebrew: אידי ואידי - רישא דעני ונמצא עשיר, וסיפא דאין לו שפחה ויש לו — תרוייהו לשבח ממון הוא. כיון דגלי ר"ש פלוגתא ברישא, לא איצטריך למהדר אפלוגי בסיפא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:9:2.english: Both this and that - The first clause of “poor and was found to be wealthy,” and the latter clause of “he has no maidservant and he has [one]” — both of them are [matters of] enhanced monetary value. Since Rabbi Shimon disclosed [his] dispute in the first clause, it was not necessary to repeat the dispute in the latter clause.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:9:3.english: Here - In the case of [one who said: 'On condition that I am a] Levite,' and he was found [to be] a priest.

Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:9:4.hebrew: דשבח יוחסין הוא - ואיכא למימר דמודה ר' שמעון בהא, משום ד״מסאנא דרב מכרעאי״ הוא. אם איתא דפליג ר' שמעון עליה — נתנייה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 49a:9:4.english: Where it is enhanced lineage - And one can say that Rabbi Shimon concedes in this [case], because it is [a case of] “a shoe that is larger than my foot.” If it is so that Rabbi Shimon disagrees with him, let [the Mishnah] teach it.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 49a:10:1.hebrew: מאי מגודלת גדלת - פי' הקונטרס: חשובה, ומתוך שהיא חשובה בעיני האנשים, דבריה מקובלים. ורבינו חננאל פי': מגדלת שער, כמו "מגדלא שער נשייא" (חגיגה דף ד:); ומתוך שהולכת מבית לבית לקלוע, מספרת כל הדברים ממנה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 49a:10:1.english: "What is megudelet? Gadlet" - Rashi explains: [She is] important; and since she is important in the eyes of people, her words are accepted. And Rabbeinu Chananel explained: [It means] a braider of hair, like "a braider of women's hair" (Chagigah 4b); and since she goes from house to house to braid [hair], she recounts all matters concerning her.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 49a:11:1.hebrew: המתרגם פסוק כצורתו - פירוש: כמשמעותו, כגון "לא תענה על ריב" מתרגם "לא תסהיד על דינא" — הרי זה בדאי, דאדרבה, מצוה הוא להוציא הדין לאורה; אלא הכי מתרגם: "לא תתמנע מלאלפא למאן דמתבעי מינך בדינא". "והמוסיף עליו" — פי' בקונטרס: שבא לומר: הואיל וניתן רשות להוסיף, אוסיף אני בכל מקום שארצה — "הרי זה מחרף", פירוש: מבזה את השם, משנה את דבריו. ואונקלוס שהוסיף, לא מדעתו הוסיף, שהרי בסיני ניתן התרגום, שנשתכח וחזר ויסדו, כדאמר במגילה (דף ג.). ורבינו חננאל פירש: "המתרגם פסוק כצורתו", כגון "ויראו את אלהי ישראל" (שמות כ״ד:י׳), דמתרגם "וחזו ית אלהא דישראל" — הרי זה בדאי, דשכינה ממש לא ראו, דכתיב (שם לג): "כי לא יראני האדם וחי"; "והמוסיף עליו", דאמר "וחזו ית מלאכא דאלהא" — הרי זה מחרף, שתולה שבח המקום במלאך; אלא הכי מתרגמי': "וחזו ית יקרא דאלהא דישראל":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 49a:11:1.english: "One who translates a verse according to its form" - Explanation: According to its literal meaning. For example, [if for] "You shall not speak in a dispute" [Exodus 23:2], he translates, "You shall not testify in a lawsuit" — this is a liar, for on the contrary, it is a mitzvah to bring the judgment to light! Rather, this is how it is translated: "You shall not refrain from teaching anyone who seeks [instruction] from you in a lawsuit." "And one who adds to it" — Rashi explained: who comes to say, "Since permission was given to add, I will add anywhere I wish" — "this one is a blasphemer," meaning he disparages God, altering His words. And as for Onkelos, who added, he did not add of his own accord, for the translation was given at Sinai; it was forgotten, and he returned and established it, as [the Gemara] says in Megillah (3a). And Rabbeinu Chananel explained: "One who translates a verse according to its form," for example, "And they saw the God of Israel" (Exodus 24:10), where he translates, "And they saw the God of Israel" — this is a liar, for they did not see the actual Divine Presence, as it is written (ibid. 33:20): "For man shall not see Me and live"; "and one who adds to it," who says, "And they saw the angel of God" — this one is a blasphemer, for he attributes the praise of the Omnipresent to an angel. Rather, this is how we translate it: "And they saw the glory of the God of Israel."

Tosafot on Kiddushin 49a:1:1.hebrew: שיכול לעשותו פשוט - פי' בקונטרס: אי משום שיש אויר בין שיטה לשיטה כשפושטו — אין לחוש, שיש סופרים הרבה שאינם אומנים לסדר כתיבתן ומניחין אויר בין השיטות. ונראה, דאפי' יש חלק הרבה — אין לחוש; ואע"ג דגט קרח פסול, לא מיקרי קרח אלא כשיש שיטות של חלק טפי מן העדים החתומים בו, אבל אם יש עדים החתומים בו כשיטות של חלק — לא מיקרי קרח:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 49a:1:1.english: “Because one can transform it into an ordinary [document]” - The Kuntres explained: If [the concern is] because there is blank space between line and line when one unfolds it, there is no concern, as there are many scribes who are not skilled at arranging their writing and leave blank space between the lines. And it appears that even if there is much blank space, there is no concern. And even though a “bald” bill of divorce is invalid, it is not called “bald” unless there are blank lines in excess of the witnesses signed on it; but if there are witnesses signed on it corresponding to the blank lines, it is not called “bald”.
